reviewer: same retained original code-blind F36/Fly visual judge
scope: Visible carried-body pose readability and gross interpenetration only; prior P2-119 issue
comparison_limits: Different land stands 16m apart and different capture adapters/native1920-normalized versus native1280; six supplied rasters are1280x720. Pose-read comparison only, not exact pixel matching.
preference: NONE for airborne carried-body improvement; A has the clearer supplied grounded endpoint
reason: No convincing visible improvement to the prior P2-119 rigid hanging/grip issue is established. In both sets' views1 and2, the trainer torso remains upright, legs hang nearly straight and the arms are raised beside the head; hands lie near Galecrest's outward talons. The bird retains an upright torso above the trainer, so the relation still reads like a bird perched near raised hands instead of a convincing supported carrying grip. No clear knee tuck or substantial carried-body silhouette change is discernible between A and B in these frontal views.

frame_specific.finding: Whole bird and trainer are visible, with separated wing silhouette and readable faces. Rigid upright trainer/dangling legs and raised-hands/talon relation remain. No obvious gross aerial body interpenetration or frame-edge cropping is established; small hand contact is too limited to certify detailed grip geometry.

The same carried-body and grip readability problem remains. Whole aerial bodies fit the frame; no persuasive knee-pose improvement is visible. Background placement differs and cannot be treated as a pose/material change.
Whole grounded trainer is readable in the grass; Galecrest is absent. Supplies a grounded endpoint only, with no bird landing/perch pose or transition.

Trainer boots overlap/sit above another person's hat/head in projection, obscuring normal ground contact and compromising the grounded endpoint. Galecrest is absent. This view does not establish a landing transition.

limits: Two glide snapshots plus one grounded endpoint per set only. Staged carrier/unlock/canopy override: no earned travel, campaign reachability, continuous motion, landing transition, co-op, full F36#1, full matrix or release acceptance claim. Absence of gross penetration in the aerial stills is not full deformation validation.
